name: BWSSB Rainwater Harvesting & Groundwater Recharge Incentive
funder: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB), Govt. of Karnataka
why: Location, community applicant type and proposed water harvesting works match listed rules under the Karnataka Municipal RWH Mandate.
checks: Within BWSSB service boundary and BBMP municipal zones.
Registered resident welfare association (RWA) or housing society.
Rooftop rainwater harvesting, dual-piping and percolation recharge wells.
Falls within state municipal subsidy guidelines.
Current financial year window is active and accepting community bids.

name: Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban) & AMRUT 2.0 Community Recharge Scheme
funder: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India
why: Co-funding grant for urban watershed restoration and community stormwater injection projects.
checks: Augmenting local groundwater and reducing non-revenue water loss.
Community contributions co-financed up to 50% by central/state allocations.
Detailed plan and verified demand reduction baseline required.
Implementation schedule within 90 days of grant sanctions.

name: National Water Mission Catch the Rain Grant
funder: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India
why: Supports community-level artificial recharge, rooftop storage structures, and desilting of catchment pits.
window: Catch The Rain Phase V · Active
checks: Conforms to Central Ground Water Authority guidelines.
Requires pre- and post-construction GPS coordinates verification.
Co-funding commitment by applicant resident association.

name: Tata Trusts Community Water, Sanitation & Recharge Programme
why: Grants targeted at high-stress water zones for community rainwater harvesting, recharge wells, and local water security.
checks: Matches designated southern water-stress priority districts.
Society registration certificate and PAN details must be submitted.

name: India Water Portal & Arghyam Community Aquifer Grant
funder: India Water Portal & Arghyam Open Water Network
why: Scientific advisory and grant support for participatory aquifer recharge, soil filtration, and open recharge wells.
checks: Site must feature suitable soil permeability for infiltration.
Requires at least 25% community own contribution commitment.

name: Karnataka Ground Water Authority Recharge Subsidy
funder: Department of Water Resources, Govt. of Karnataka
why: Incentive for housing societies constructing artificial recharge structures in notified critical ground water assessment units.
checks: Within over-exploited or critical groundwater assessment taluks.
Adheres to Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) artificial recharge manuals.
Self-declaration and layout plan approval from municipal authority.
